hourly.summary: Manchester United drew 1-1 with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford after conceding a 92nd-minute Solanke header, extending their worst start in 40 years to six points from six games. The boos rang around the Theatre of Dreams as Carrick's side yet again failed to see out a game against a reduced opponent, leaving INEOS weighing up the manager's future while fans chant 'we are fucking shit' into the void. The only positives? Baleba's debut, Yoro's minutes, and Kobbie Mainoo continuing to be the sole functioning organ in a body that's forgotten how to run.

daily.summary: Sentiment remained consistently negative across the day, anchored by a worsening injury crisis (Sesko, Amad, Rashford, Dorgu, Mazraoui, Mainoo all doubts), striker impotence, and deep frustration with INEOS ownership. Early-morning grimness over a wonderkid exit and City schadenfreude gave way to midday lineup anxiety, then deepened into evening panic after another poor showing left fans duct-taping the back four and begging for January.

weekly.summary: The week began with fleeting schadenfreude over Manchester City's 115 charges but rapidly curdled into a sustained cycle of aggrieved grievance — fixated on INEOS ownership, institutional bias, and United's own injury crisis. A brief mid-week recovery fueled by the women's derby win and transfer optimism proved short-lived, as the period closed in grim resignation: toxic outrage at Zirkzee and the regime settling into gallows humor that masks a fanbase that has normalized mediocrity and a 13-year title drought.
